newsitem.title: USA: Miami official denies bribery allegations.
newsitem.headline: Miami official denies bribery allegations.

text.p: Miami City Manager Cesar Odio denied allegations Monday that he was involved in a scheme involving bribes for city contracts.
"I have nothing to be ashamed of," Odio told a news conference at his attorney's office. "The facts will come out and I will be proven totally innocent."

No charges have been filed against Odio or anyone else. The Miami Herald and several local television stations have reported that federal bribery charges are pending against Odio, City Commissioner Miller Dawkins, former city Finance Director Manohar Surana, lobbyist Jorge de Cardenas, and possibly other local government officials.
The U.S. Attorney's Office declined to comment.
At a city budget meeting Monday, Dawkins said he had no first-hand information on any pending charges. He said he knew only that the newspapers were "reporting I did something."
"Once they show me what it is, I'll get back to you," Dawkins told city officials at the meeting.
Surana and de Cardenas have declined comment.

Surana resigned unexpectedly Aug 30. Miami Herald reported that he allegedly accepted a $2 million bribe in connection with a computer system sold to the city, then agreed to wear a hidden wire to tape conversations implicating other city officials.
Cardenas is the owner of Creative Marketing and Advertising Group. He lobbied the city on behalf of a company that won a contract to provide health insurance to city workers.

If Dawkins resigns or is indicted and suspended by Gov. Lawton Chiles, the city commission would have 10 days to choose a new commissioner or call a special election. It would also be up to the commission to find a replacement for Odio.
Deputy Finance Director Dipak Parekh was appointed acting finance director after Surana resigned.
